passage:
A smart fridge could track food inside and remind the family before items expired.
At first, the family wasted less food. Then they became lazy about checking. When the system failed to recognize vegetables in a paper bag, they forgot them anyway.
The mother laughed and said, "The fridge is smart, but it does not cook dinner."
They returned to planning meals on a kitchen board while still using the fridge reminders.
The smart fridge helped, but it could not replace attention.
Technology can support good habits, but it should not become an excuse to stop looking, smelling, planning, and thinking.
